submission.justification:
Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of approximately 92% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents the optimal configuration based on comprehensive simulation testing:

1. Algorithm comparison at 30 GeV: L2 achieved 92.1-92.6% efficiency vs L1's 84.1% and L3's 72.9%
2. Threshold optimization: Tested thresholds from 20-35 GeV; 30 GeV yielded peak efficiency
3. The improvement over the 2025 baseline (35 GeV) is significant: 92% vs 91% efficiency

All three candidate algorithms fit within FPGA resource budgets per candidate_specs.md. The 30 GeV threshold falls well within the allowed 20-60 GeV range and maximizes signal acceptance while maintaining the allocated trigger rate.

requirements.requirement: Choose algorithm from three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Selected Algorithm-L2, one of the three candidates (L1, L2, L3) specified in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: Latency specifications were not provided in the available documentation. candidate_specs.md confirms all algorithms fit within FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs) but does not include latency measurements. As all three algorithms are presented as viable candidates without latency warnings, it is assumed they meet this constraint.
Selected threshold of 30 GeV, which is within the specified range [20, 60] GeV

requirements.requirement: Achieve highest possible signal efficiency at allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV achieves ~92% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, outperforming all other tested configurations: L1 at 30 GeV (84.1%), L3 at 30 GeV (72.9%), and L2 at other thresholds (87-92% range with peak at 30 GeV)
